implementation_notes: Spring Integration makes the invalid channel a bean: an exception raised by an asynchronous component becomes the payload of an ErrorMessage sent to the channel named by the request message's errorChannel header, or to the global errorChannel bean - by default a PublishSubscribeChannel with a LoggingHandler subscriber. Subscribe an endpoint (typically ErrorMessageExceptionTypeRouter) to spread conversion and validation failures over dedicated channels; since 5.4.3 the default channel is configured with requireSubscribers = true, so an error can no longer vanish when nobody listens. Java 17 is the documented baseline of Spring Integration 7.1.
pitfalls: Messaging-based error handling only applies to components running on a TaskExecutor; a DirectChannel handler that throws propagates to the caller and never reaches errorChannel.
requireSubscribers = true protects against silent drops but means a stopped error endpoint now negatively acknowledges or rolls back the original message, so restart ordering matters.
The ErrorMessage carries the failed request as a property; handlers that mutate or resend it can re-inject the invalid message into the original flow.

variants.name: Spring for Apache Kafka DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer (dead letter topic)
variants.implementation_notes: On Kafka the invalid channel is a dead-letter topic: DefaultErrorHandler retries with a BackOff and then hands the record to a recoverer, and DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer publishes it - the raw ConsumerRecord included, when rawRecordHeader is enabled - to <topic>.DLT. The framework already classifies conversion failures as fatal: DeserializationException, MessageConversionException and ConversionException skip retries and invoke the recoverer on the first failure, which is exactly invalid-message semantics. Choose this variant when the transport is Kafka and offsets, not queue semantics, define delivery.
pitfalls: Only RuntimeException subclasses pass through DefaultErrorHandler; an Error aborts the consumer and skips recovery entirely, so application exceptions must be classified deliberately.
Fatal exceptions skip retries, so adding a transient network exception to the not-retryable list sends recoverable records to the dead-letter topic.
The dead-letter topic keeps the original record, so an unmonitored DLT accumulates raw invalid payloads indefinitely - it needs an owner and a retention policy.
